utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I understand there are some preliminary matters. Let us deal with them as quickly as possible. Who is first?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I guess I can go first. I do need to go into private session to deal with the first matter that I have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam, with respect to the road from -- or the route of these school bus from Rujiste to the school, what route did it take, and what is the approximate distances between the various villages that are located there, and with respect to the ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From our village, Rujiste, we traveled three kilometers to the village of Klasnik where we went to the first four grades of primary school, and then after that, up to the eighth group, we went to Prelovo, which was some 10 kilometers away, and we took the bus, and then we went to secondary school in Visegrad, which is about 20 kilometers away from our village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, as far as the route taken by the students to get to the school and eventually to get to Visegrad, what is the order of the villages along the road, starting out from Rujiste heading towards Visegrad? What villages would one have to pass on the route to school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Rujiste, Klasnik, Prelovo, then there are some small hamlets, Koritnik and Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And now this route taken by the students and then by the bus when you went to the other school, is this a paved road or some other type of route?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was not paved. I don't know how I can explain it. It was cobblestones.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where there any other roads leading to Visegrad from Rujiste?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. It was the only road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned the village of Koritnik. With respect to Koritnik, was it possible to go through Rujiste to Visegrad by any other route other than the route you described?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. That was the only road you could reach Visegrad by.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, with respect to the time period that you spent with Mr. Milan Lukic in school --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'd ask first of all for Exhibit 65 ter 39 to be call up. That should be number 1D 22-0282, a document received by the Defence in response to a request for assistance of the Bosnian organs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I'll ask you to review the same and once it comes up and tell me if it comports or reflects your recollection of the time period that Milan Lukic attended school and the specific nature of his studies there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cole.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour. There has been some correspondence with the Defence on the issue of exhibits in relation to the schooling. I note my learned friend has indicated a request for assistance by the Bosnian organs. I wonder if we could just clarify that, is this document in response to an official request for assistance to the Bosnian authorities and return to the Defence through official channels or some other way because the correspondence that we've had with the Defence indicates that this document or certainly a similar one was handed over to a member of the Defence team at the school. So it's a little bit ambiguous, the explanation on the record at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'd be happy to explain, Your Honour. I've done it so again on multiple occasions. We requested this document of the school district in Visegrad, that is to say that the Defence officially requested it. The official organs of the school tendered a response to it, a written response, which was handed to members of our Defence team and which we have. It was stamped by the school, et cetera. I don't know what further information is required by the Prosecution. Not with respect to this document, but with respect to another document, I've time and again encouraged them to contact the school to verify that what I've said is accurate. I will note that with respect to the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So the answer is it's the official organs of the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: There's no other way for me to get that [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's it. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And madam, I think I've already asked you to review this document and see if it -- and I've lost my question, see if -- if it comports or reflects your recollection of the time period that Milan Lukic attended that particular school and the specific nature of his studies there according to your knowledge.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that he attended that school, but I don't know precisely what subjects he took.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. If we can -- I guess we have to tender this one before we go to the next one.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Could we tender this one as the next available 1D exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be given Exhibit 1D 105. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If we can go on to the next exhibit. It should be 65 ter number 40, and it ought to be at 1D 22-0281, and these will be the records from the -- from the earlier -- the elementary school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I would ask the same, for these records if you would take a look at it and see if it comports with your knowledge and recollection of the time periods when Mr. Milan Lukic attended elementary school, and that would have been the matters that you discussed earlier in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cole.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes. I wonder, Your Honour, if we could just have on the record where the document has come from.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do I need to read the document, Your Honour, or does it speak for itself?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Is it the same kind of information you need as to whether it's official or a government document or what?

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I don't wish to take up a lot of time, but there has been considerable correspondence, and it hasn't been clear until now where these document have come from. So if it's been handed over personally, fine. It's been suggested in the past that the documents have come as a result of an official request for assistance, and I just want to be clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: How did you get this document? Was it the result of an official request for assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will read the document then: "Pursuant to Article 159 of the law on general legal procedures (Official Gazette of the Republika Srpska, number 13/02) and on the request of Rasic Jelena from Belgrade, we issue the following." So the school organs of Visegrad upon a formal request from the Defence issued this document, and I'd be happy to provide any other information for you. That's a formal request from the Defence team to a formal organ. If you want to zoom in on the stamp, you'll see stamp issued as a -- that the stamp on this document is a formal official stamp from a state organ, that is to say, the school authorities in Visegrad of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, just so it's clear, the approach that the Prosecution has taken has to mark these documents for identification and then on paper provide the Chamber with the copy of the correspondence, the request not simply to a local grammar school in the area where the accused lives that may have a bias one way or the other, but to the official representative of the government to the Tribunal. That person then goes and does some investigation and returns with whether or not they can satisfy a request. So in many ways, an official request if I assistance as the imprimatur of the government when it goes and it finds a particular document, which these documents do not have. While they may be requested by Ms. Jelena Rasic by the local grammar school principal, they are not the same as an official request by the Defence to an official representative of the Tribunal. So I ask that they be marked for identification and then -- and provide the same underlining documents that the Prosecution has and intends to with the remainder of the documents that it will introduce so that the Court can assess what was requested, what was returned, and make its own assessment as to whether the document should be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's a tenant of many jurisdictions including this one that public documents obtained from public officials can even be introduced via the Bar table, not even through a witness. The document speaks for itself as to what was requested. It provides data based upon the official records of the school and is signed by an authorized official of the school and stamped by an official of the school. I don't see what more -- if Mr. Groome is contending that depending on who you ask for documents from there's a bias, then how do we ever know any document arising from there is not subject to a bias? Who's the official that the Prosecution asks for these documents from? These documents were requested whether orally or in writing from an official, and we received the documents, and the official has identified the school at issue. It has a stamp. That can all be contacted and checked. Again, we're running into this issue where we have these individuals on our witness list. We took them off the witness list based on the understanding that the documents received from officials were to be used --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, let me see if I understand it. You would have contacted --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The school in Visegrad, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... the primary school, Vuk Karadzic, and asked for information concerning the accused and the director, who is Mr. Slavco Sandev, he produces this document. He prepares it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And how does he prepare it? By doing what?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, as the custodian of the records of the elementary schools in Visegrad from the time period when the accused attended school, he would go to the archives, review the archives --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: All that information is not there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, I return to the point then again. We had these people on the witness list, but we have been asked to do 45 witnesses. If I have to bring records custodians in for documents when the Prosecution submits wholesale documents without records custodians, some of these that they claim that they seized somewhere, that they don't even know who generated them, I don't know how to proceed. We have to take into account fairness of the proceedings, we have to take into account efficiency of the proceedings and ensure that justice is undertaken. Again, they've known about this document for some time. I've invited them to contact the school officials on numerous occasions, and, Your Honour, if I may make a segue into this, the Prosecution requested the original of another document that came from the school. I did not have that original initially. I obtained that original. Made a meeting with the Office of the Prosecution. What did the Office of the Prosecution do with respect to that original? They asked for a photocopy of it, which is the same thing they've had since day one. So really I think -- I submit that the Prosecution is really just trying to do -- is trying to stall these proceedings by objecting to these documents that can be verified on the face, and they speak for themselves in terms of the information that they contain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It may be that it comes down to a question of the weight to be attached to it, you know, in the absence of other confirming information.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I'd be more than happy to call the records custodians, as long as they don't count as one of my limited, very precious 45 witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: All right. We'll admit the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Actually, I don't know whether the witness has already answered with respect to this document, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: All right. Go ahead and ...

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam, with respect to this document, I would ask that you look through it and tell us whether this comports with your knowledge and recollection of the time period when Mr. Milan Lukic attended the elementary school Zelimir Djuric - Zeljo.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This document is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now I would submit this document for the next 1D exhibit, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: When you say it's correct, what do you mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is correct that he enrolled in the 1st grade in that year, just as it says here, and he went to school, Zelimir Djuric, Zeljo, in Prelovo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Cole may have some questions. Go ahead. We'll admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be given Exhibit 1D 106. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Madam Witness, with respect to these proceedings, we've had some witnesses come and tell us some things about how they were able to travel to and from school from various villages, based upon your knowledge of the area, is it possible to have children from Koritnik go to school in Prelovo but to have them go through Rujiste to get to the school in Prelovo? Was that one of the routes of transport that was available during the time period when you and Mr. Lukic were attending school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's impossible to go through Koritnik and past Rujiste in order to get to school. That is incorrect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, during the time period that you knew -- strike that. During the time period that you attended school with Milan Lukic, did you ever have occasion to witness him smoking cigarettes or any other type of tobacco?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he never smoked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With respect to the time period when you were -- when you knew Milan Lukic and when you were travelling to school with Milan Lukic as well as in school, how would you describe his interactions and behavior with regard to other persons, be they children or adults, be they Serb or non-Serb?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He always behaved very well towards Serbs, Muslims, older people. He was always cheerful. He never caused anyone any problems.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you already mentioned -- strike that. With respect to when the children would socialise, did you ever have occasion to eye-witness Mr. Milan Lukic initiating a fight or roughing up other kids?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. He never engaged in quarrels. He was always in good company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Based upon your knowledge and information as to Milan Lukic gained from the time period that you spent with him and knew him, how would you -- how would you describe for us his character? What type of person is he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Very positive person, upbeat. I can only say the best things about him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what kind of student was he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good. Average, I would say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And with respect to -- with respect to Mr. Milan Lukic, when is the last time that you personally saw Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In 1984, I left. Then I came back in 1986. That was the last time I saw him. I've not seen him since.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Based on your contacts with your own relatives, et cetera, and your knowledge, did Mr. Milan Lukic remain in Visegrad municipality upon the completion of the schooling?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I learned that he was in Switzerland for a while, and later he lived at Bezanijska Kosa in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. With respect to -- strike that. Let me just -- with respect to the kids in school when you were growing up, did -- hang on one moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of activities would Milan Lukic be involved in during the breaks in school between classes, if you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He would play along just like all the other kids.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if we can just briefly go back into private session for one or two other questions that might otherwise reveal personal information about the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam Witness, I thank you. I have no further questions on direct for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I pass the witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cole.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour. Yes, Your Honour. I have some questions that I would ask that we go into private session for.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cole.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Could we go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you were shown some documents from schools that were attended by Milan Lukic in your testimony earlier. Do you recall those documents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, those same documents, they were shown to you during the course of your proofing earlier today. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when they were shown to you in this courtroom, you had already refreshed your memory from the information contained in them, hadn't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if you're going to be fair, you would have to accept that without the information that was contained in those school documents, you would have no idea about any years that -- specific years that Milan Lukic attended any school.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's true that he started school the year I said, 1974.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember -- you were asked if the contents of the school certificates were correct in terms of information about Milan Lukic. Do you remember being asked that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you confirm that the information in those two school certificates was correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So can you tell us now what the information is that you confirmed was correct. Can you remember it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It said that he started school, the first grade of elementary school in Klasnik in 1974. I confirm that to be true.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And Your Honour, I had to check the transcript, and I had to object to Mr. Cole's question as far as they misstate the question that was asked. I specifically asked if it comports with her knowledge and recollection of the time periods that Milan Lukic attended elementary school, and that's at page 23, lines 4 through 8.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cole.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour. I'm going to move on from that topic now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, you left primary school and moved on to secondary school yourself in what year?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you at secondary school with Milan Lukic on any -- in any year?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but not in the same school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what secondary school did Milan Lukic attend?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He first trained to become a waiter, and then the next one had to do with technology.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember which secondary school he attended?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were separate schools, but both were in Visegrad. I don't know what the name was of the school that he went to. I don't remember, actually.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you were at school, were you friendly with other children who were Muslim children?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I'm not going to ask you to say them now, but do you remember the names? If you were asked, could you remember the names of a number of Muslim children that you went to school with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So I'll just ask you about some names here and see if you might be able to help with these. Did you know any Muslim children by the name of Kurspahic when you were going to school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So how many years were you at secondary school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Four years.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't remember anyone by the surname of Kurspahic while you were at secondary school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Anyone by the name of Kurspahic while you were at primary school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know someone by the name of Jasmina Delija, D-e-l-i-j-a, while you were at school, either primary or secondary school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Changing the subject now, when you were you first contacted by the Milan Lukic Defence in relation to this trial or evidence or testimony that you may give?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In October 2008.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And by what means were you contacted?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: His sister asked me whether I would agree to make a statement about our socialising and going to school together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the name of his sister?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Draginja.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where does she live?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in October, how did she make contact with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: She rang me up on the telephone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean that she has been in regular contact with you over the years that she has your telephone number?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, as she got my telephone number from my family.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So did you agree to speak further with members of the Milan Lukic Defence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the next contact you had from anyone about this trial?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Only the lawyer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So after October, when was the next contact you had from this lawyer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In January of this year.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So no contact at all with anyone until January of 2009, nothing at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the contact you had, was that from -- well, who was that from, which lawyer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The lawyer. I've forgotten his name now. That lawyer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that Mr. Ivetic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Seems you are imminently forgettable, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that contact in January, was that phone call, or was that a personal call -- a personal meeting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In January, we met in person.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the date of that meeting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know precisely, between the 15th and the 20th, thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you make a written statement that you signed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. We only talked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you were firstly scheduled to testify in this trial last week, weren't you? That was the original plan? Have I got that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was it Monday or Tuesday last week that you were originally scheduled to testify?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what's the reason that you weren't able to? We may --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: I think it would be appropriate for closed session for that answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. Actually, I don't -- well, go ahead. We'll go into closed session. It doesn't matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Closed session, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, when was the last time that you saw Milan Lukic in person?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you specifically seek him out, or did you see him by chance on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I came to Bosnia to stay with my mother, and then I saw him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it just on the one occasion in 1986?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And have you seen Milan Lukic since that day in 1986?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But did you recognise him when you walked into court first thing this afternoon for the first time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you, in fact, smiled at Milan Lukic, didn't you, and he smiled back at you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in your testimony earlier, I think you said that when you knew Milan Lukic he was not a smoker, didn't smoke cigarettes. Have I got that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I can't remember if you were asked about whether he was an alcohol drinker at the time when you knew him, but -- so I'll ask you now. Did he, as far as you know, in the years that you knew him, up until -- was it 1984, was he a person who would drink alcohol regularly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So I'm just going to ask that a photograph be shown to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And the reference number is Y014-7901.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you see that photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you see a cigarette in the hand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you can confirm that's a photo of Milan Lukic, can't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll just ask you if you could now be shown a photograph Y014-7908. Can you see Milan Lukic in this photo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you can confirm that is some alcohol that he has in the bottle in his hand.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection. Calls for speculation.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: How are you able to say that it is alcohol in the bottle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it looks like it. When he went to school, he neither smoked nor drank. These were probably special occasions when that took place, or I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, just from a perspective, obviously, that Mr. Cole has not put a time and place and year and otherwise established to the witness that the last time she saw him was in 1986, which by math, would have been the year Mr. Lukic graduated high school and around that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. These are photographs that were supplied by the Milan Lukic Defence, so they would certainly be in a better position than anyone to provide a date for these photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, other than them coming from the -- you know, the personal files of the family or what-not or the collection of the family, unless it's stamped on the photograph as was the first photograph we showed, D -- I guess it was D 190 had a date on it from the camera, but we can only assume that the person who programmed the camera did it correctly, but on these photographs there was no such time stamp on the photos. We would have to put Mr. Lukic on to establish all of them, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cole. Proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just finally on the photograph that you're looking at now, on the question of alcohol, does that bottle in Milan Lukic's hand appear to be a common type of beverage available in the Balkans?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know Milan Lukic's parents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where his mother is at the present time, Milan Lukic's mother?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: His mother and his father are currently in Belgrade. Not currently, what I mean is they live there now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you believe that his father is still alive?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Could we briefly go into closed session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Your Honour, a matter to ask, the two photographs shown to this witness and which you identified be tendered as exhibits. Could I ask that they both be given exhibit numbers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be give the following exhibit numbers: Document Y014-7901 shall be assigned Exhibit B 231. Document Y 014-7908 shall be assigned Exhibit B 232. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in your testimony earlier you described Milan Lukic as positive, upbeat, and you said that you can only say the best, and you said also that he was always in good company. Do you remember saying those things about Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So as you are testifying here today, you're saying that you only know good things about him, positive things, and that's the image of him that you would wish to portray to the Court?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And since 1986, what contact have you had with Milan Lukic until today?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No contact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you're aware of the war in Bosnia and the former Yugoslavia, and no doubt you were able to read about that in newspapers and watch it on the television news at the time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what years is it your understanding that the war -- what years the war continued through from start to finish?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know precisely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, during the war and in subsequent years, did you read in the newspapers or see on the television news items about Milan Lukic in particular?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would it be fair to say that you were aware that he was a fugitive and finally arrested in 2005?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I heard that in the media.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as you sit there, are you aware that Milan Lukic faces serious charges in this court, including extermination and many murders?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know that it is alleged that he has murdered scores of persons, including putting people in houses and incinerating them to death?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you don't know those allegations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Many people have testified about his misdeeds in this court. Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection, relevance, improper foundation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I don't see the basis for the objection.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The question is, Are you aware that many people have testified in this court about his misdeeds, if I can call it that. You're aware of that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you say, do you, that he's a good man, still say that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. He was like that when I knew him. I wasn't in the war. I don't know what was going on at the time, but the only Milan Lukic I know is a good and positive person.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know anything about the time that Milan Lukic returned from elsewhere in Europe to Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know anything as to the circumstances surrounding Milan Lukic's return to Visegrad during the war in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You see, that proposition I just put to you is included in a document provided to the Office of the Prosecutor by the Defence in describing your testimony. Do you have any comment to make about that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I see Mr. Ivetic on his feet. Yes, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I object as to the relevance. I object as to the foundation, again, as to what the witness knows what the Defence is presenting based on the limited [indiscernible] we have on that time, and I believe she has already testified as to the extent of the contact that she had during the time when the witness lists were generated when she was contacted and asked whether she would agree to testify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So what's the relevance of this, Mr. Cole?

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Well, we're provided, of course, with very little information about a witness anyway. This is an official document submitted by the Defence about what the witness is intended to testify about, and I put the exact words from it to the witness, so the relevance is, firstly, that we've been supplied with information that appears to be correct, and I believe I'm entitled to ask the witness about a summary of her evidence here, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: I see, Your Honour, that she has answered the question, in any event. She's -- well, if I could just read the question again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "You see, the proposition I just put to you is included in a document provided to the Office of the Prosecutor by the Defence in describing your testimony. Do you have any comment to make about that?" And that question relates to the suggestion you would testify as to the circumstances surrounding Milan Lukic's return to Visegrad during the war. So any comment about why that would -- that comment would be included in your proposed testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in your testimony earlier, page 30, you testified that you learned that -- or you were aware that Milan Lukic went to Switzerland at one stage. Who did you learn that from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My relatives from Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: If we could just go into closed session briefly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: I'm going to ask that the witness be shown, I think it's Exhibit 1D 90.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you were shown this photograph before by counsel. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you pointed out one person, and was that Novica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is that the person, Novica Lukic, the person on the immediate left?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So just have a look at the other persons on the photograph. I don't know that your attention was drawn specifically to them. Can you see the other persons in the photo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't really recognise. Maybe the second one on the right is Milan, but I'm not certain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Have you seen that photograph before, before today?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: If I could just have a moment, Your Honour, I've managed to cut down the questions that I was intending to ask, and it may be that I have just a couple more, if any. Yes, just a couple more, Your Honour. If we could go into closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Madam, we're almost there. Just a few more questions on my side at least. Now, you've been asked by the time period in the tenth month of last year when you were contacted by the Defence to give testimony in this case. At that time, did anyone from the Defence have occasion to come meet with you and interview you about the extent of the your knowledge that you could offer as testimony in these proceedings?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cole.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes. Even though it's re-examination, of course the rules relating to leading evidence still apply, and I would just ask my learned friend if he could refrain from leading when he's putting questions to his witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, the fact that it's a yes or no question doesn't mean that it's leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. I agree. It's not leading, and it arises from cross-examination. Yes, please answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, moving on, madam, I understand the math problem. Sometimes we're all bad with figures and with adding and calculating, especially when it comes to years. But just to be clear, during the years when Milan Lukic was attending school in Visegrad, whether that was in Klasnik, Prelovo, or Visegrad itself, how were you travelling to your school? By what means?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: By bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And how was Milan Lukic travelling and attending his school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The same means.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And am I to take that to mean that you were on the same bus?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And with respect to that bus, would it drop -- would it drop students off at the schools that they attended?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And so for the time period that you testified about when you went to school with Milan Lukic -- strike that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I think that's made my point, Your Honour. I think the rest would be just pure adding, overstepping. Madam, I thank you for coming here to testify in these proceedings, and on behalf of the Milan Lukic Defence team, I thank you very much for the effort and time to testify and for coming here. Thank you. No further questions for this witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Witness, that concludes your evidence. We thank you for coming to the Tribunal to give it. You may now leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, the next witness is MLD4. I don't know, are we scheduled for a break or ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The break is usually at 35 minutes after 5. It's 25 minutes to 6. Do you want us to take it now?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If it pleases Your Honour, I could take the break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. All right. We'll take the break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let the witness make the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ivetic. You may begin.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Good day, sir. As you know, my name is Dan Ivetic, and I'm one of the attorneys for Milan Lukic's Defence. I have to refer to you today as MLD4 to be in line with your protective measures. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: I understand fully.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: At this time, with the assistance of the court usher, I would ask for the pseudonym sheet document to be handed to you, and sir, when you have an opportunity to review this document, I would ask that you look at the same and verify that the information contained on it as to yourself - that is, your name, last name, and date of birth - is correct.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: The information is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. If you could please sign -- thank you, sir. If you could please sign the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And then, Your Honours, I would submit this is the next -- to be tendered as the next available 1D exhibit in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be given Exhibit 1D 107 under seal. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Register. I'd forgotten that should be under seal. That's correct. Is the witness having difficulty with the translation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The right speaker isn't working properly.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: How about now? Is it working now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you sir. For the time being, we are in public session, meaning that everything you are saying is being transmitted, so I would urge you to be careful when answering my questions so as not to reveal your identity, and the first question I have for you is, What ethnicity are you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: I'm a Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And which of the former Yugoslav republics were you born in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: Bosnia and Herzegovina, what is now Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd ask now to go into private session to keep protected the identity of the witness on the next several questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, after being mobilised, what type of tasks were you given to undertake?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: Well, in the direction of my village, there were guards there. On the other side down there, there is Zepa, Pripecak, and some other places where people thought the Muslim forces couldn't get there to burn down the villages, and so we held those guards there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. In the course of performing your guard duty, did you wear a uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And were other persons in Visegrad being mobilised in that area around the same time that you had been mobilised?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: I think they called up everyone in the space of one or two days.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And with respect to the command, where was the military command located in the Visegrad area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: It was at Bikavac.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Where specifically in Bikavac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: In a hotel called Bikavac.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay, and was there also a kitchen where food was prepared for the army, the Territorial Defence, and the police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And where was that kitchen located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: In that restaurant of that hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, while you were doing guard duty, did you have occasion to go to the military command's kitchen to eat, or was food provided by other means?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: First, we got dry food for a certain time, and then they started bringing cooked food to the lines in a vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You say that at a certain point in time cooked food was being brought to the lines. From where was this food being brought?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: I think from the kitchen at Bikavac.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you recall who it was, that is to say, the persons who delivered the food by vehicle to the lines?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: It was brought by Stevan or Steva, I think his name was Vukovic or Milosavljevic, and Josip.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And what type of -- and what type of vehicle would these persons utilise for delivering the food to yourselves and others on guard duty and to the lines?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: Sometimes it was a van, and sometimes it was a TAM truck, a small one.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And these persons, Stevan or Steva or Josip, were they persons who participated in combat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: No, they were at the kitchen at the command, and they only took care of the food for the soldiers and distributed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If I can have an exhibit shown to the witness. I believe it's marked in e-court as P 229. And if we could zoom in on the photograph on this picture -- on this page.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to ask you to take a look at this photograph and tell me whether, in fact, you can recognise any of the two individuals that are depicted on this photograph.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Could you tell me -- could --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: This one to my right is Steva or Stevan, and the other one is Josip.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And for the record, when you say that these are Steva or Stevan and Josip, are these the same individuals that you have described for us previously who worked in the kitchen at the military command?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, can you recognise the vehicle that is depicted in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: What can you tell us about the vehicle in this photograph, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: Well, that's the vehicle, and those two men, but not on the side where I was, on the other side, when they were driving the food up to the men, they ran into an anti-tank mine, and then they and the vehicle got blown up.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you indicated that these men were attached to the kitchen at the military command. To your knowledge, were either of these two men ever members of the so-called White Eagles?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: As far as I know, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we could focus for a moment, the gentleman on the left-hand side of the picture. I forget. Could you tell us who that is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: To my left?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: That's Josip.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And for the record, what kind of hat is Josip wearing in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: It's the sajkaca hat.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And what kind of a hat is a sajkaca? Who is it usually worn by?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: Well, you'll see that usually in Serbia, around Uzice, that area down there, and it's worn by Serbs, Serb farmers or peasants as they call them.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: With respect to Josip, what kind of name is Josip and what religious affiliation is he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: Well, I never talked about it with him, but judging by his name I think he was a Croat.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And are you familiar with his family? Who was he married to, for instance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: I know his wife, and he had two daughters.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: What was the name of his wife, and how was she employed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: I think she's retired now, and she used to work in the health centre. She was a nurse, and her name was Vida Stjepanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you know what village the wife of this gentleman Josip is from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: A village near my village. Its name was Paocici.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's all I have for the picture. That can be taken off the screen now.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Now, if we could focus on yourself for the time being, during the course of the time that you were mobilised into the Territorial Defence in Visegrad, did you have occasion to participate in any actions in addition to the guard duty that you were performing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: On one occasion up there opposite were I was, the place is called Kopito.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, with respect to this one occasion in Kopito, do you recall when that was precisely?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: That was on the 13th of June, 1992. Yeah, I said 2002 again. I apologise. It was 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, could you detail for us how it was that you came to be involved in this action in the region of Kopito in Visegrad municipality beginning the 13th of June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: A Lada Niva came, and the commander told me to get in the car and we should go because we needed to go up to Kopito, as the Muslim soldiers were passing on the Gorazde-Zepa, Zepa-Gorazde road, and they had even set fire to some houses up there, and we had to set up an ambush.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, when you say a Lada Niva came, where were you when the Lada Niva came for you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: I was at the position down there, at Rujiste.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And when you say you were told to get in the car, was anyone else in the car with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: Yes, two others as well. That's what the komandir told us, You, you, and you go, but he didn't tell us where we were going. He said, Get in the car and go to the command.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And then what happened? Where did the car take you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: They took us to Bikavac, in front of the command.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: What approximate time of day was this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: In the morning at around 9 or 10 a.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, what did you see when you arrived at the command at the Hotel Bikavac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: I saw more soldiers and policemen gathering there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Were there any persons among the soldiers and policemen that were gathering there whom you recognised?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: I recognised Milan, whom I saw for the first time after that conflict, there in front of the command I saw him.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Line 7 of page 73, I believe the witness said "before that conflict."

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, when you say Milan, to which Milan are you referring to, if you could please be specific?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: Milan Lukic. I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And just so that we're abundantly clear, which -- which of the Milan Lukices from Rujiste did you see on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: The one we see here now with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Is there a problem? Okay, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: First of all, before we get to the specifics of this encounter and the Milan Lukic that we see here before us today, what can you tell us about the other Milan Lukic from Rujiste?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: That was an elderly man who was killed I think in 1993, down there below his village. He was an older man, 60 or so.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honours. I'm having to deal with an inquiry from VWS at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, now, if we could focus back on the -- on your arrival before the command on the 13th of June, 1992, wherein you saw Milan Lukic and you said it was the first time you'd seen him. Were you surprised to see Milan Lukic at that time there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: Yes, I was, because I hadn't seen him since the conflicts began, and I hadn't seen him for some time before that either.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And when you saw Mr. Milan Lukic there in front of the military command on the 13th of June, 1992, with whom was he in the company of?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: He was with a group of men who were wearing camouflage uniforms, and it said "milicija" on their left shoulder.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And just for purposes of clarification for those of us that don't speak B/C/S or Serbian, the term "milicija" is reflected in the transcript. At that time, what organisation was called the "milicija"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: Well, today it's called the police. I don't know what else I could say. It's the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Now, could you tell us, then, what happened. Did all of you remain there, or were you told to go elsewhere? What happened after you arrived at the command and saw Milan Lukic with other persons in the uniform of policemen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: We arrived there, we said hello, and then we waited for further orders. We were given orders to get in the cars there and go to Kopito.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, you had indicated earlier that when you arrived you saw more soldiers and policemen gathering there. Approximately how many of these soldiers and policemen received this order to get into the cars and go to Kopito?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: Well, perhaps about 20 men.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And what happened then? Did you actually have occasion to set out for Kopito?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: Yes, we did. We got into the vehicles and arrived up there at Kopito where we were met by local people. Among them was Vlatko Tripkovic. I didn't know him, but he introduced himself. He said he was Vlatko Tripkovic, the commander of that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Who was it that gave you instructions once you arrived at Kopito as to what -- as to where you should go and what you should do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: There was a lad there with Vlatko who introduced himself as Novica Savic, and he told us where those men were passing by and where we should -- where we should take up our positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if we could back up just for a second. Could you tell us what happened to Milan Lukic. You had seen him at the command. Did you see him again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: Yes, yes. He was with us, with me, in that same group of men.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: What about when you arrived at Kopito? Where was Milan Lukic at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: He was with me. We socialised a bit because we knew each other, so we decided to stick together.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, after introducing themselves and telling you where you should take up your positions, what did the persons, Tripkovic and Savic, what did they then do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: Tripkovic said he had to go to Visegrad to the command for a briefing. Perica Markovic took over the command, so he was there to supervise us, deploy us, and give us further instructions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did, in fact, Tripkovic set out for Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: I didn't know that at the time, but the next day I learned he had set out. He was killed somewhere along the way.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Just waiting for the transcript and the translation to catch up with us. We'll get to the next day in a moment. I want to focus first on that first day when you and the others arrived at Kopito, and first of all, could you describe for us what kind of terrain -- what kind of terrain is it where Kopito is situated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: The road from Visegrad to Rogatica is an asphalt road through the wooded area, and then there is this road that cuts across it that people from Gorazde take to get to Zepa. It's all woodlands, all around. I'm not sure if you'll understand. We call it a goat path. It's some sort of a path, so it's surrounded by a forest with all sorts of trees, small trees and some fir trees as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Again, I'm waiting for the transcript and translation to catch up with us, sir. Now, when you indicated earlier that you were told to take up positions, what type of positions were you told to take up? Where in fact did you -- were the positions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: They said we should camouflage our presence along the road that was likely to be taken by the Muslim army.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did you establish any -- strike that. Were there any houses or structures in that area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: Yes, five or six houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: At the time that you arrived at Kopito and received your instructions, were you told approximately how long your engagement on that region -- or at that location would last?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: When we first set out, they gave us some dry rations and told us that we might stay there for four or five days.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And where was it that you were to spend the night, et cetera, at Kopito?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: There were some houses there as I said in my previous answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did you in fact stay into the next day, the 14th of June, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: Yes. We still -- we stayed until the morning of the 15th.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. I appreciate that. I'd like to go back and focus on the 14th of June, 1992, for the time being. Did anything happen on the 14th of June, 1992, where you were situated in the Kopito region?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: A car arrived along the Rogatica Visegrad road driving in the direction of Visegrad. It had police plates, and Djeric was in it with another lad.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, if we could back up, there's several things there I'd like to focus on. First of all, you said Djeric was in this vehicle. Which Djeric are we talking about, or could you give us his name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: Goran Djeric.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And from whence did this car come from? What direction?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: From Rogatica.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And was there any military installment or command in Rogatica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: Yes. The Rogatica Brigade was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And with respect to the road that you've described and the terrain that you've described, where is Kopito in relation to Rogatica and Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: It's right between the two, but that's the only road connecting Rogatica and Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay, now. So Djeric arrived at your positions in Kopito coming from Rogatica in the Golf that had the police license -- registrations. What happened then? Did you have occasion to speak with him? And when I say "him," I mean Djeric, Goran Djeric.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: Well, it was by coincidence because we knew each other that I walked up to him and Milan Lukic and some other people too. Milan Lukic and I approached him, and he told us that Vlatko Tripkovic had been killed near a place called Tabla, somewhere along the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And how had Mr. Djeric obtained that information?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: Well, we had no communications equipment because all if that was in Tripkovic's car. So the Visegrad and the Rogatica Brigades got in touch because this is something that you can see from Visegrad. You could see a car burning, but one didn't know who it was or what had happened, so the Rogatica Brigade and the Visegrad Brigade got in touch. And Kusic from Rogatica dispatched Goran Djeric to convey the news to us to the effect that the next stage in operation should be launched from up there because Tripkovic had been killed. And from Visegrad those other guys should get on their way in order to clear the road to make sure the road was open and usable.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And to whom was Mr. Djeric to deliver this message?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: He asked who the commander was, who was in charge. Lukic and I went to the house where Perica Markovic was staying. We walked with him all the way to Perica Markovic, and then he conveyed the news to Perica Markovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, you've mentioned that Mr. Tripkovic was in his car and perished at the location near a place called Tabla. Could you in reference to -- in reference to Rogatica, Kopito, and Visegrad, could you tell us where Tabla is located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: That's closer to Visegrad, about halfway between Kopito and Visegrad. It may be a little closer to Visegrad than it is to Kopito.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And do you recall what approximate time of day it was that Mr. Goran Djeric arrived from Rogatica with this information?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: Perhaps about 10.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, did Mr. Djeric leave after giving his information and his instructions to Perica Markovic? Did he leave Kopito?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: He stayed with us. He stayed with us that night, and when we set out for Visegrad and the operation had been launched already, he drove back to Rogatica.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us, then, when it was that the operation was launched in terms of the day and the time of day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: We left on the morning of the 15th at about 9.00, 9.30, perhaps. That would be the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Could you describe for us how it was that you set out in the course of undertaking this operation. How did you -- how did you and the other soldiers and policemen set out along the road towards Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: We received orders to go to Visegrad because the people in Visegrad had left already in a bid to clear the road, so we walked from up there, walking more along the road than on the actual road itself, so by the side of the road, and then on to Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did you have occasion to actually meet up with the other Serb forces coming from the direction of Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: Yes. It was about noon that same day, more or less.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did you have occasion to eye-witness the site where Mr. Tripkovic and his car had met their demise?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: Yes. That was where we met up. Those other people were there already. His body was pulled out if there was anything left of his body because the car had burned down already. We met up there, and all I saw was the wreck, the car's wreck.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, did you have occasion to learn at any point in time whether Mr. -- Commander Tripkovic had perished alone or whether anyone else had perished with him on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: There were another two there: Novica Savic, and I can't remember the third man's name.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And during the time period that you were up in Kopito with Milan Lukic, do you recall the names of any other individuals that you spent a considerable portion of time during the 13th, the 14th, and the morning of the 15th in that region?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: People from the area or people who were actually with us?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Anyone that you can actually remember being with you that you could -- that you could know to name.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: Well, perhaps I could give you five, six, seven, or eight names: Milan Josipovic, Vidoje Andric, Zjelko Tasic, Gogic, Timotije Joksimovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Fair enough. We'll get back, I think, to that later. After you met up with the forces near the -- the other forces coming from the direction of Visegrad near the Tabla location where Commander Tripkovic and the others had perished, what happened then? Where did you and the other police and soldiers from -- who had come from Kopito, where did you go and by what means?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: We lingered there for a while, and then our vehicles caught up, the ones who had been driving behind us. We got into those vehicles and drove back to the command at Bikavac.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And upon -- and upon your return to the command in Bikavac, what else -- strike that. Where else did you go? What else did you do? What were you told to do at that point in time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: Well, nothing, really. We drove back in that Lada Niva that we had arrived in. They went back to pick us up and then drove us back to the line.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Did you ever have occasion after that date and after that action to participate in any other military actions with Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, do you recall what time of day it was approximately when you returned to Visegrad, that is, specifically towards the Hotel Bikavac command?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: Perhaps between 1 and 2.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Have you had occasion to -- strike that. When did you -- when did you leave Bosnia to return to your current home? What year?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: I'm not sure I understand. When did I leave Bosnia? You mean to work in Belgrade or what?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No. After the war, when did you return to Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And after that, did you have occasion to return to Bosnia and to Visegrad municipality?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And did you have occasion ever to cross the road there at Kopito -- or excuse me, pardon, at the Tabla location to see if there are any memorials or monuments in place there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD4
utterances.text: No, I never drove past. That's on the other side of the Drina River, and when I travel from Belgrade to Visegrad, I don't pass the Drina River. I just drive down the right bank of the river whenever I go to visit my mother.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, I take it that you will be concluding?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes. That was my last question, Your Honour, so I am actually finished the witness. Thank you, sir, for your time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: All right. We'll have the cross-examination tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 27th day of January, 2009, at 2.15 p.m. 21 22 23 24 25
